title: Private CP operators notebook — scale provenance and upgrade play
content:
Purpose and scope:
This operators' notebook is a working, practical companion for field engineers who run and scale Private Control Plane (CP) deployments (VPC and on-prem). It focuses on provenance for scaling decisions, safety checks for upgrades, and explicit Terraform module migration notes.

This is intentionally concise and action-oriented — think of it as the thing an on-call engineer reaches for at 2am. It is not the architecture spec or the final customer onboarding doc. It complements those by capturing the heuristics, test commands, and small scripts we use in production.

High-level goals:
- Safe scale: increase capacity without customer-visible latency spikes or state loss.
- Recoverable upgrades: every upgrade path has a tested rollback and a short verification checklist.
- Clear provenance: every capacity change is linked to an experiment or a ticket and has measured before/after metrics.
- Terraform hygiene: explicit steps for state handling, lock recovery, and module replacement during migrations.

Quick references (cheat sheet)
- Primary telemetry dashboards: Console -> Private CP -> Capacity -> token-p95, token-p99, request-rate.
- Emergency fallback model: route policy = fallback-small-llama (for tiered customers).
- TF state snapshot: terraform state pull > /tmp/tf-state-snapshot-$(date +%F).json
- Lock reclaim (if needed): aws dynamodb delete-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"<LOCK_ID>"}}'
- K8s drain with eviction grace: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120

Initial setup checklist (minimal install for a greenfield on-prem CP)
1) Prepare inventory: nodes.csv with columns: hostname, numa-sockets, gpu-type, nic-bandwidth, region-label.
2) Networking: ensure NAT bandwidth >= expected egress; run iperf3 between edge router and control plane aggregator for 30s to capture baseline.
3) Storage: mount a consistent path for runtime logs (/var/lib/redwood/cp-logs) — use ext4 with noatime for write performance.
4) Secrets: import customer KMS keys into HSM gateway and register KAS token thumbprint in the private-controlplane-secrets vault.
5) Bootstrap: run ./bin/cp-bootstrap --inventory nodes.csv --tf-state s3://redwood-private-cp-states/teams/<team>/state.tfstate --dry-run then remove --dry-run if no errors.
6) Smoke test: POST /healthz on API gateway, ensure kv-cache warmup returns >=30% hit rate after synthetic pre-warm flow.

Scaling playbook (horizontal + vertical)
- When to scale: p95 token latency sustained above SLO for 15m or queued request growth > 20% for 10m. Link metric to ticket and run provenance checks below.
- Horizontal (add worker pods or nodes):
  * Start with a canary increment: add 10-15% capacity in single AZ/row.
  * Monitor p50/p95/p99, token-cost per request, and kv cache hit ratio every 60s.
  * If p95 increases after new nodes added, suspect cold-KV warming or imbalanced routing — roll back and try warmed node pool (see KV warming).
- Vertical (bigger GPUs / bump vCPU):
  * Prepare a test tenant with production-weight traces replayed locally (use 30m window sampled percentiles).
  * Confirm kernel-level NUMA settings: set GOMAXPROCS and enable hugepages where supported.
  * Apply one instance at a time to avoid large capacity gaps.

KV cache warming strategy (common cause of post-scale latency)
- Always pre-warm new nodes: replay most-recent 2% of requests from request-log-store into a warm-up agent. Command: ./bin/warm-kv --target node-ids --window 30m --rate 50rps
- If replay not available, use prefix-scan synthetic generator keyed to high-frequency prefixes (anonymized) to raise hit ratio to >60% before adding to routing pool.

Provenance for scale decisions (how to record)
- Create a ticket: CP-SCALE-YYYY with fields: baseline snapshot id, proposed delta, reason, expected cost delta.
- Attach telemetry snapshot: export dashboard JSON and include persistent link.
- Annotate terraform plan: run terraform plan -out=plan-CP-SCALE-YYYY && terraform show -json plan-CP-SCALE-YYYY > plan.json and attach plan.json to the ticket.
- Post-change: capture prometheus snapshot and a trace sample for the time window of change; compare to baseline and summarize in the ticket.

Terraform module migration notes (common pitfalls)
- Always run terraform providers lock file refresh before major module changes.
- Module replacement pattern (safe):
  1) Introduce new module with _staging suffix and point to new module source (git tag).
  2) terraform apply on staging module only, ensure new resource names are distinct.
  3) Migrate state for selective resources: terraform state mv old_resource new_resource.
  4) Validate in staging pool for 24h under partial traffic.
  5) Remove old module in a follow-up change.
- State drift: if drift detected, snapshot state and open a ticket CP-TF-DRIFT with diffs. Do not attempt to import resources without approval.
- Lock recovery: if Dynamo lock left after crash, confirm active pipeline ID then delete lock entry manually. Record the deleted LockID in the ticket.

Upgrade plan (control plane minor version X.Y -> X.(Y+1))
- Pre-upgrade:
  * Run full integration tests in staging with synthetic load 30% of production.
  * Create backup: pg_dump for metadata DB, rsync for node volumes, and terraform state snapshot.
  * Verify canary tenant: pick an internal canary customer with low criticality and run upgrade there first.
- Upgrade steps:
  1) Drain one CP node and cordon it.
  2) Apply package upgrade; run post-install smoke script.
  3) Monitor metrics for 30m: p50/p95, error 5xx rate, KV hit, CPU steal.
  4) If green, uncordon and proceed to next node.
  5) After 25% of nodes upgraded, run full integration smoke (end-to-end inference trace).
- Rollback triggers: any sustained p95 regression > 20% vs baseline for 15m, or error-rate spike > 2x baseline.
- Rollback procedure: redeploy previous package from artifact repo (artifact tag pinned in ticket), drain upgraded nodes and roll back, restore DB backup only if corruption detected.

Rotation and evacuation patterns (for emergency maintenance)
- Partial evacuation (turndown of one AZ):
  * Update routing policy to prefer other AZ and set fallback ramp at 20% for 10m.
  * Gradually drain nodes in the affected AZ with 2-minute intervals between nodes.
  * Continuously monitor request queue depth and p99.
- Full evacuation (data center evacuation): follow the evacuation-runbook checklist in Confluence and notify security + infra leads.

Observability gating and acceptance criteria
- Before promoting canary or scaling change to full fleet, the following must be green for 60 minutes:
  * p95 token latency within 10% of baseline
  * 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.1% or absolute 0.2% whichever larger
  * KV cache hit ratio >= baseline - 5%
  * No recurring terraform lock failures during apply windows

Common troubleshooting snippets
- High p95 after new nodes added:
  * Check kv cache hit per node: /internal/metrics/kv-hit?node=<id>
  * If hit low, confirm warm-up completed and routing weight for node is <= 5% and only ramping up slowly.
- Terraform plan hangs on provider auth:
  * Recreate credentials in vault, run aws sts get-caller-identity to confirm.
- Node shows elevated CPU steal:
  * Check host-level co-tenancy or scheduling; if bare-metal, inspect NUMA pinning and interrupt affinity.

Postmortem anchors (what to capture in CP incident writeup)
- Timeline with exact terraform apply/run ids and git commits.
- Before/after metric snapshots (attached as JSON).
- Root cause hypothesis with short test plan for validation.
- Cost impact (tokens, infra) and mitigation steps.

Appendix: short scripts and commands
- Snapshot plan + push to ticket:
  * terraform plan -out=plan.bin && terraform show -json plan.bin > /tmp/plan-$(date +%s).json && gh issue comment CP-SCALE-YYYY --body-file /tmp/plan-$(date +%s).json
- Warm-kv manual replay (example):
  * ./bin/warm-kv --target node-1,node-2 --window 45m --rate 100rps --auth-token $WARM_AGENT_TOKEN
- TF lock reclaim example: (ONLY after verifying there is no active pipeline)
  * LOCKID=$(aws dynamodb scan --table-name tf-locks --filter-expression "contains(Info, :runid)" --expression-attribute-values '{":runid":{"S":"$RUN_ID"}}' --query 'Items[0].LockID.S' --output text)
  * aws dynamodb delete-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"'"$LOCKID"'"}}'

Open questions / follow-ups
- Experiment to validate cold-start token-cost penalty per model family under varying KV warm percentages (Maya to run A/B tests, CP-SCALE-EXP-11).
- Document controlled airgap build iteration for edge customers: current packaging time is 4.5 hours; target <2 hours.
- Evaluate an automated pre-warm step integrated into the terraform lifecycle so nodes come up already registered as warm in routing.

Notes on provenance and citations:
- When in doubt, always link a terraform plan output and the metrics snapshot to the ticket. That evidence is the provenance trail for audits.
- If you deviate from this notebook during a live incident, add a short note to the ticket describing the deviation and the reason.

End of operators notebook — leave feedback or update this doc when you discover a new pattern (please add a short changelog entry at the top and ping #private-cp-ops).
